I have resolved the issue where proxy authentication resulted in HTTP 407 errors.

### Root Cause
In commit `ef59aa02`, [`prepend_scheme_if_needed`](file:///testbed/requests/utils.py#L960) was updated to parse URLs using urllib3's `parse_url` instead of Python's `urlparse`. In `urllib3.util.parse_url`, the returned `netloc` attribute contains only host and port (without userinfo), and authentication credentials are stored separately in `parsed.auth`.

When reconstructing the URL with `urlunparse`, `auth` was omitted from `netloc`. Consequently, whenever `prepend_scheme_if_needed` was called on a proxy URL containing authentication (e.g. in [`HTTPAdapter.get_connection`](file:///testbed/requests/adapters.py#L305)), the user authentication credentials (`user:password@`) were stripped from the proxy URL. When [`HTTPAdapter.proxy_headers`](file:///testbed/requests/adapters.py#L373) subsequently attempted to extract proxy authentication via [`get_auth_from_url`](file:///testbed/requests/utils.py#L985), no credentials could be found, resulting in an omitted `Proxy-Authorization` header and HTTP 407 response from authenticated proxies.

### Solution
Updated [`prepend_scheme_if_needed`](file:///testbed/requests/utils.py#L960-L983) in [requests/utils.py](file:///testbed/requests/utils.py) to preserve `auth` by prepending `auth + '@'` to `netloc` when present before passing it to `urlunparse`.
